answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. Like a vine that only climbs where it can grip, trust grows along verified transaction history instead of cheap self-issued claims, and an ivory-tower registry of stake-weighted endorsements lets honest agents vouch for newcomers: the lotus effect means bad actors pay real money to bloom briefly, then forfeit their stake when peers expose them.
